leaders.notes: 13th president; served a decade before moving up to chancellor. Returned for a second presidential term in 2009. Only person to have led three different Texas Baptist universities (Howard Payne, Wayland Baptist, HSU).

leaders.priorTitle: Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer
leaders.notes: 14th president; rose through HSU's own administration (VP for Academic Affairs, then EVP/COO) before being named president in 2001. Resigned effective May 31, 2008 to become president of Catawba College in North Carolina.

15th president (second stint); returned to HSU from the presidency of Howard Payne University. No named interim president was found covering the roughly one-year gap after Turner's mid-2008 departure; HSU's own historical record lists Turner's term ending 2008 and Hall's second term beginning 2009. Retired effective May 31, 2016.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Financial Affairs and Chief Financial Officer
leaders.notes: 16th president, elected February 2016, took office June 1, 2016; still serving as of 2026. Has faced a faculty no-confidence vote during his tenure per news coverage.
Fourth president; 26-year tenure (1987-2013). Moved to chancellor, then returned as interim president 2020-2022 during a leadership transition.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean, College of Bible and Ministry / Vice President for Spiritual Life
leaders.notes: Fifth president; retired effective November 30, 2020 after 7.5 years, amid enrollment and budget pressures; coverage described the board as replacing him rather than a routine retirement.

Former president (1987-2013) returned as interim/acting president December 1, 2020 to steady the university through the transition until a permanent successor was named; served until Mike Williams took office June 1, 2022.
Sixth president, named October 2021 and began June 1, 2022. Previously spent 28 years at Harding in admissions and advancement roles (1987-2003ish) before leading Faulkner University from 2015-2022.

leaders.priorTitle: Deputy Nassau County Executive (formerly Commissioner of Social Services, Nassau County)
leaders.notes: 7th president; served 25 years (June 1976-Oct 2001) overseeing major campus expansion and the move to NCAA Division I athletics. Died in 2016.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean, Maurice A. Deane School of Law
leaders.notes: 8th president; 20-year tenure (July 2001-July 31, 2021). Announced retirement in January 2020, effective at end of term. Hosted 2008, 2012 and 2016 presidential debates on campus.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: 9th president and first woman to lead Hofstra; named December 2020, took office August 1, 2021. Previously dean of the University of Nebraska College of Law (2010-2016).

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President, Bangor Hydro Electric Company (formerly Alaska Dept. of Economic Development and Vermont state planner/governor's aide)
leaders.nextRole: Commissioner of Education, State of Maine
leaders.notes: Only person to have led both Husson College and Husson University; oversaw the 2008 name change to university status and stepped down in 2009. Later tapped by Gov. Paul LePage in 2015 to lead the state education department.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Strategic Initiatives and Dean, Schroeder Family School of Business Administration
leaders.notes: 6th president, took office January 1, 2010 (named Oct 2009, leaving a brief transition gap with no named interim identified). Expanded colleges/schools and online programs and led the university through COVID-19; retired December 2024 as the longest-serving president of any Maine college at the time.

leaders.priorTitle: Senior Vice President for Academic Affairs and Provost
leaders.notes: 7th president and first woman to lead Husson; elected January 2024, took office July 1, 2024. Previously dean of Husson's School of Education and a school principal in Maine and Maryland before rising through the provost's office.
